summary: Canada beat Jamaica 2-1 in the first leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal in Kingston, with Stephen Eustaquio's 85th-minute goal following Jonathan David's first-half stoppage-time opener and Shamar Nicholson's equaliser. The match was moved to Saturday after heavy rain flooded Independence Park on Friday. Canada will qualify for Copa America 2024 if they avoid defeat in the second leg at BMO Field in Toronto.
one_line: Canada won 2-1 at Jamaica in the Nations League quarterfinal first leg, moving close to Copa America 2024 qualification.
key_facts: Canada beat Jamaica 2-1 in the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal first leg, their first win in Jamaica in 35 years.
Jonathan David scored in first-half added time (45+2), his 26th international goal, from a Cyle Larin turn and cross.
Shamar Nicholson equalised for Jamaica in the 58th minute after an initial offside call was overturned by VAR and referee Mary Penso's pitchside monitor check.
Stephen Eustaquio scored the winner in the 85th minute from a Richie Laryea run and low pass; it was his first international goal since 2021.
The match was postponed from Friday, November 17 because heavy rain flooded Independence Park in Kingston, and was replayed at 10:30am ET on Saturday, November 18, 2023.
Canada will qualify for Copa America 2024 if they avoid defeat in the second leg at Ontario's BMO Field on Tuesday.
Nations League semifinalists qualify for Copa America; the losing quarterfinalists play off for two remaining spots in March.
Leon Bailey hit the post from a Bobby Decordova-Reid corner in the first half and missed other good early chances for Jamaica.
Michail Antonio left injured in the first half with a possible hamstring problem and was replaced by Trivante Stewart.
Canada had 11 of the 16 first-half attempts and four of the five on target.
The win ended Canada's two-match losing run and was their second win in seven matches.
Jamaica had never won in Canada; Canada had won only one of their last 11 visits to Jamaica.
Official attendance was a little more than 3,500.
Canada's interim head coach Biello said his players were on a 'mission', and John Herdman had recently left the Canada job.
